items.name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Fancy Dress
items.body:
A Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj fancy dress for kids, shown on a boy and laid flat. The set in the flat photo is a cream and gold printed angrakha with a layered, flared hem and gold borders, a wide red sash for the waist, red pyjama, a pearl mala and the tall, cone-shaped Shivaji pagdi in cream and gold with red bands. On the boy it is styled with a curved sword, which is not in the flat set: ask us on WhatsApp, or add our dhal and talwar set.

It is the look children need for Shivaji Jayanti (19 February), Maharashtra Day (1 May), history dramas and fancy dress competitions on great Indian rulers. Add a drawn-on beard and moustache and a short line from his life, and the character is clear from the back of the hall. Tell us your child's age when you book and we will confirm the fit.

items.name: Mexican Fancy Dress for Girls
items.body:
A Mexican fancy dress for girls in the folk style, shown on a girl and laid flat. It is a turquoise blue, ankle-length dress with a wide gathered skirt, a white lace yoke edged in orange and red ribbon, and elbow-length sleeves finished with ribbon bands and lace frills. Bands of pink and white ribbon run around the skirt, with red and orange ribbon and a white ruffle at the hem. Add a flower in the hair, as in the photo, for the full look.

It suits international day, "countries of the world" and "Unity in Diversity" themes, a Mexican folk dance item at the annual function and world cultures week at school. A few lines such as "Hola! I am from Mexico, the land of mariachi music and colourful fiestas" make the act. Tell us your child's age when you book and we will confirm the fit.

items.body:
An Indian Army dress for kids in the camouflage print often called the "Kargil print". The set is a full-sleeve uniform shirt with four flap pockets, shoulder straps, an embroidered "Indian Army" badge and a tricolour strip above the pocket, matching trousers and a camouflage cap. Add black shoes and a smart salute, as in the photo, and your child is a fauji ready for the stage.

It is one of the most asked-for costumes for 26 January Republic Day, 15 August Independence Day, Kargil Vijay Diwas (26 July), Army Day (15 January) and "our heroes" or community-helper fancy dress competitions, and it works for a group soldier dance too. For a class or house group, WhatsApp us the number of children and their sizes. Tell us your child's age when you book and we will confirm the fit.

An Assamese dress for boys, made for Bihu and state-day programmes. The shirt is cream with rows of red Assamese motifs, a maroon mandarin collar and button placket, and patterned half sleeves; it is worn over a white dhoti with a yellow border down the front pleat. In the photo the boy wears cream mojaris, which complete the look.

It is a clear, easy-to-recognise choice for Rongali Bihu in April, Assam or North-East theme days, "Unity in Diversity" and states-of-India fancy dress competitions, and a Bihu dance item at the annual function. Add a japi (the Assamese bamboo hat) or our Assam cap if you want a prop. For girls, see our Assam saree (mekhela chador). Tell us your child's age when you book and we will confirm the fit.

A Bengali boy fancy dress in the dhoti-kurta style worn for Durga Puja. The set is a red kurta with a mandarin collar and gold-trimmed placket, a white dhoti with a red and gold border down the pleats, and a white uttariya (stole) edged in gold that drapes over one shoulder. In the photo it is worn with gold mojaris.

It suits Durga Puja and Poila Boishakh programmes at school, West Bengal or states-of-India fancy dress competitions, "Unity in Diversity" days and a Rabindranath Tagore-themed recital. A short line about Bengal's festivals or its poets is all the act needs. For girls, see our Bengali saree costume. Tell us your child's age when you book and we will confirm the fit.

A Bharat Mata (Mother India) dress for girls. In the photo the girl wears a white saree with a red and gold border, the pallu over the shoulder and a gold waistband, with a jewelled gold crown, red and gold bangles and the Indian flag in her hand. It is the most recognised patriotic costume on stage, and it pairs well with a short poem or a single line such as "I am Bharat Mata, and every child of India is mine."

Choose it for 26 January Republic Day, 15 August Independence Day, desh bhakti dance items and freedom-fighter fancy dress competitions. For a Republic Day group item, WhatsApp us the number of girls and we will check stock. Tell us your child's age when you book and we will confirm the fit.

The set is a green full-sleeve jumpsuit with elastic cuffs and ankles, an orange carrot-shaped panel on the front with brown ridges and a leafy green top, tied at the sides, and a green cap with three standing leaves.

It suits vegetable and healthy-eating theme days, nursery and kindergarten fancy dress, nutrition week and annual day group items alongside other vegetables. A Haryanvi daaman dress for girls, the folk outfit of Haryana. The set in the photo is a white full-sleeve collared shirt, a full green daaman (flared skirt) with two silver gota bands and a pink hem, and a pink odhni with a silver lattice and border, worn over the head. The flat photo also shows a silver coin necklace and a pair of kadas with the set, and the girl wears a maang tikka and earrings.

It is a natural choice for Haryana Day (1 November), Teej, states-of-India fancy dress, Haryanvi folk dance items and "Unity in Diversity" theme days. For a group dance, WhatsApp us the number of girls and their ages. Tell us your child's age when you book and we will confirm the fit.

items.body:
A dhal and talwar (shield and sword) set for stage battles. The dhal is a round black shield crossed with two silver bands, with four silver studs, a domed silver boss in the centre and a silver rim. The talwar is a curved silver sword with a gold hilt, a knuckle guard and a red tassel at the grip. Both are drama props.

It completes a warrior look in Ramleela battle scenes and Dussehra plays, and it suits Rani Laxmi Bai, Shivaji Maharaj, Maharana Pratap, Rajput and Maratha costumes for history dramas and fancy dress competitions. Raise the sword and hold the shield across the chest for the classic warrior pose. If you are booking a full costume as well, tell us and we will keep the set with it.

A Hanuman Ji costume for Ramleela and Dussehra plays. The outfit is red with wide gold borders: a short-sleeved top with "Ram" written in pearls on the chest, a gold-trimmed waistband with hanging panels, and knee-length shorts banded in gold. In the photo it is completed with a tall red and gold crown, a monkey face mask over the mouth and nose, a long red-and-gold tail with a black tuft, an orange gada, and pearl malas, bracelets and anklets.

It suits Ramleela and school Ramayan plays, Hanuman Jayanti, Dussehra and Diwali functions and mythology fancy dress competitions. A line such as "Jai Shri Ram" with the gada raised says the rest. Tell us your child's age when you book and we will confirm the fit.

It suits Raja Dashrath, Raja Janak or any king in Ramleela and Dussehra plays, Rajput and Maratha kings in history dramas, and "kings and queens" fancy dress competitions. The black choli has a silver and gold yoke, coin trim at the neckline, rainbow ribbon bands at the sleeves and a frilled peplum. The full-flare black lehenga is worked with a silver lattice, wide bands of yellow, orange, blue, pink, red and turquoise ribbon and round mirrors, and the black dupatta has a gold fringe and colourful pompoms. The flat photo also shows a coin necklace and two kadas with the set.

It is made for Kalbelia and Rajasthani folk dance performances, college fests, Rajasthan Day and cultural programmes, where the skirt shows off every spin. For girls, see our Kalbelia dress for girls. Send us bust, waist and height measurements when you book and we will confirm the fit.

The kediyu (the flared garba top) has a mandarin collar, a yoke of green, blue and maroon peacock embroidery covered in small mirrors, mirror-work cuffs and a full, flared skirt with flower embroidery, mirrors and a maroon border. It is made for Navratri garba and dandiya nights, school garba competitions and Gujarat or "Unity in Diversity" theme days. The photo shows it on a girl, and the same set suits boys. The kediya is also spelt kedia or kediyu. Tell us your child's age when you book and we will confirm the fit.

items.body:
A Mughal king costume for kids, made for school history skits and fancy dress competitions. On the boy in the first photo it is a magenta and gold brocade angrakha with gold borders and tie fastenings, a red sash at the waist, a white brocade dhoti with a striped border, pearl malas and a gold turban with a jewelled band and white feather, held with a gold sword. The flat photo shows a pink angrakha with gold borders and red ties, a red sash, a cream dhoti and a gold pagdi with red and green trim.

It suits Akbar, Shah Jahan and Babur roles, Mughal-court acts at the annual day and "kings and queens" themes. Tell us your child's age when you book and we will confirm the version and size we have for your date.

items.body:
A Rani Laxmi Bai pagdi for girls: a red turban wrapped in neat folds, with a wide gold floral border band across the front. It is the headpiece that turns a saree or drape into the warrior queen of Jhansi on stage.

Use it for freedom-fighter fancy dress, 19 November (Rani Laxmi Bai's birth anniversary), 26 January Republic Day, 15 August Independence Day tributes and school history dramas. Pair it with a sword and shield, such as our dhal and talwar set, for the "Khoob ladi mardani" pose. For the full outfit, see our Jhansi ki Rani dress for girls. Tell us your child's age when you book and we will check the fit.

items.body:
A tiranga (tricolour) costume for kids, with a version for boys and one for girls. The boys' set is an orange sequin waistcoat over a white full-sleeve top, with harem pants in white and green sequins gathered at the ankle. The girls' version is a frock with a ruffled orange bodice, a silver sequin waistband with orange side ties and a three-tier shiny green skirt. In the photos the boy has tricolour face paint and the girl wears tricolour wristbands and hair clips.

Both fit 26 January Republic Day, 15 August Independence Day, desh bhakti dance items and patriotic fancy dress competitions, and they look striking in a group. Tell us whether it is for a boy or a girl, and the child's age, when you book.
